Candidate rules for clean + "just works":

**Code quality**
1. **Lint/format gate** — run formatter (black/ruff) + linter before done. Zero warnings. Single enforced style = no drift.
2. **Type hints everywhere** — full annotations, `mypy --strict` (or pyright) must pass. Catches whole bug class before runtime.
3. **No dead code** — unused functions, imports, variables, files deleted on sight (within task scope). `ruff --select F401,F841` or vulture.
4. **Complexity cap** — function over ~40 lines or nesting >3 deep must split. Keeps everything readable without comments (fits Rule 2).
5. **Naming convention spec** — snake_case funcs, SCREAMING constants, no abbreviations, names must state intent. Self-documenting code is what makes Rule 2 viable.

**"Just works" reliability**
6. **One-command setup** — `make setup` or `setup.sh` installs everything from clean machine. If new dep added, setup script updated same session.
7. **One-command run + one-command test** — `make run`, `make test`. Agent must verify both still work after each task (catches "works on my edit" breakage).
8. **Pinned dependencies** — exact versions in requirements.txt/lock file. No `>=`. Reproducible = no surprise breakage.
9. **Fail loud** — no bare `except:`, no swallowed errors, no silent fallbacks. Validate inputs at boundaries, crash with clear message otherwise.
10. **No hardcoded paths/secrets** — config in one place (single config file or env), all paths relative to repo root.

**Process**
11. **Atomic commits** — commit after each passing work unit, message says why. Easy rollback when something breaks.
12. **Pre-done checklist hook** — before declaring done: lint clean, types clean, tests pass, setup/run/test commands verified. One mechanical gate catches everything.

Biggest wins: **2 (types), 6–7 (one-command everything), 9 (fail loud), 12 (final gate)**. Want me add some or all as Rules 8+?
